title: Career Switch into Full-Stack Development
excerpt: James left retail at 34 with no coding background. Four months and one bootcamp later he accepted a junior developer offer with a 40% salary lift.
content:
James was a retail store manager who had never written a line of code. His motivation was concrete: a junior developer role paid 40% more than his current salary, and the skills were in demand on every skilled occupation list.

He joined our full-stack bootcamp with three commitments: four hours of study each weekday evening, pair programming on Saturdays, and a project every two weeks.

Months one and two covered JavaScript, HTML, CSS and React fundamentals, with weekly code reviews. James's biggest hurdle was debugging — he would stare at broken code instead of reading the error message. A three-step debugging checklist fixed that in a fortnight.

Month three was the back end: Node, PostgreSQL and REST APIs, capped with a full stack project: an inventory app for his old workplace, with auth, search and reporting.

Month four was portfolio and interview preparation: two more projects, live coding practice and mock technical interviews every week. He applied to forty roles, interviewed at nine, and accepted an offer from a Melbourne fintech at 40% above his retail salary.

James's advice to others switching careers: build something real every two weeks, get your code reviewed by a professional, and treat the job search as a full-time job from month three.
